rule: Exclude any identified full proof or disproof claim for the exact question, regardless of acceptance. A result only for a special class, fixed dimension or asymptotic weakening is not a full resolution.
limitation: Bounded literature, problem-page, forum and web searches; no claim of exhaustive absence. Some broad queries returned irrelevant matches, so source pages and exact-scope follow-ups were checked.

retained.scope_note: The problem page highlights k=3. The formalization retains the entire original progression-length family. Constant-factor comparison is partial.
Formalizes the positive answer to the original question. The 2026 linear upper bound with coefficient 3/10 is partial, not a resolution.
Original question on printed p.251. Equal-distance pairs may share an endpoint; restricting to four distinct endpoints would weaken it.
The 2026 paper proposes a stronger conjecture, not a proof. Structured matrix and small-order results do not settle arbitrary normal pairs.
Known low-dimensional results do not resolve all dimensions. Distinct from Brunn–Minkowski and Minkowski lattice-tiling conjectures.
All graph orders retained. Verification through order 48 and later restrictions are partial.
Both the inequality and its original equality clause are retained. Two-block and low-rank results are partial. Different from the Marcus–Minc transform conjecture, now claimed proved.

Formalizes the negative answer to the original zero-permanent existence question. Finite-order checks and the all-order Sylvester result are partial. Other solved Wang questions about resemblance classes or maximum permanents are different.

apparent_claims_reviewed.finding: Boundary-matrix theorems and conditional reductions. Section 7 still states two unproved conjectures; not a full Marcus–de Oliveira proof claim.
Sections 6.1–6.3 explicitly restrict the claimed resolution to circulant convolution operators, which commute. Does not claim all normal pairs.
Explicitly restricted order-seven rank-three Chollet inequality; not either selected permanent question.
All Sylvester Hadamard matrices, not all real Hadamard matrices.
Solved Wang/Perfect question about resemblance classes with equal permanent differs from nonvanishing; finite-order nonvanishing is partial.
Wang–Kräuter maximum-permanent-at-fixed-rank question; not Hadamard nonvanishing.
